basis: Book III's two consecutive paragraphs begin with the Mark 10:42 lemma about rulers among the gentiles, explain the abbreviated 10:43-44 comparison with humble service, and then quote and expound the Son of Man's ransom at 10:45. The preceding paragraph treats 10:41 and the following one begins 10:46. The complete natural unit is therefore Mark 10:42-45. Exact Latin substrings from retained digital-witness lines 312-313 were checked against PL92 col.236A-B (retained image artifact.jacques-paul-migne.patrologia-latina-volume-92.paris-1862.ia-leaf-n122-4cdb234f); the generated extraction prefixes are omitted and the source's etc. abbreviation is preserved. The digital expression is not silently identified with that 1862 printing. The existing page-only 1862 passage witnesses the same text and stays unmapped. Use beside a weekly study's Matthew 22 reading is a study-specific analogue, not direct Matthew commentary. Bede's prefatory distinction between inherited patristic material and his additions remains; individual sentence origins are not newly authenticated.
date_basis: The composition date of this commentary has not been established from the witnesses actually read for this batch. The retained Latin dedicatory preface at raw line 3 describes the earlier Luke exposition only in relative terms and provides no calendar year for the Mark exposition; the checked Mark 10:42-45 block likewise gives no composition year. On 2026-10-23 the primary CNRS/IRHT Bibale and FAMA catalogue pages could not be acquired directly (timeouts/HTTP 403); their indexed 725-730 estimate remains an unadopted lead, as recorded in artifact.cnrs-irht.bibale-bede-in-marci.2026-10-23-web.bibale-entry-39610. No author death, printing, retrieval or inferred calendar date is substituted. This is a bounded statement about the project's reviewed evidence, not a claim that scholarship knows no date for Bede's work.
text: Jesus autem vocans eos, ait illis: Scitis quia hi qui videntur principari gentibus, dominantur eis, et principes eorum potestatem habent ipsorum. Non ita autem in vobis, etc. Humilis magister et mitis, nec cupiditatis immodicae duos arguit postulantes, nec decem reliquos indignationis increpat et livoris, sed tale ponit exemplum, quo doceat eum majorem esse qui minor fuerit, et illum dominum fieri qui omnium servus sit. Frustra igitur aut illi immoderata quaesierunt, aut isti dolent super majorum desiderio, cum ad summitatem virtutum non potentia, sed humilitate veniatur. Denique sui proponit exemplum, ut si dicta parvi penderent, erubescerent ad opera. Et dicit: Nam et Filius hominis non venit ut ministraretur ei, sed ut ministraret, et daret animam suam redemptionem pro multis. Nota quod crebro diximus, eum qui ministraret, Filium hominis appellari, et dare animam suam redemptionem pro multis; quando formam servi accepit, ut pro mundo sanguinem funderet. Et non dixit, dare animam suam redemptionem pro omnibus, sed pro multis, id est, pro eis qui credere voluerunt.
